Query SAP HANA as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__hana.R
oauth_db_hana.Rd

Open a DBI connection to SAP HANA or SAP HANA Cloud using the visitor's JWT access token. HANA maps the token's external identity to a database user and applies that user's privileges.

Usage

oauth_db_hana(
  authorization,
  server,
  database = NULL,
  ...,
  port = 443L,
  schema = NULL,
  driver = "HDBODBC",
  ssl_trust_store = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

server

One HANA SQL endpoint hostname or IPv4 address, without a protocol or port.

database

Optional tenant database name. NULL uses the database selected by the SQL endpoint. HANA Cloud normally needs only its endpoint.

...

Result options timeout, timezone, timezone_out, bigint, encoding, name_encoding, and interruptible. Native authentication, routing, reconnect and TLS settings cannot be overridden.

port

SQL endpoint port, default 443 for HANA Cloud. For self-hosted HANA, use the SQL port supplied by your administrator.

schema

Optional initial SQL schema. NULL uses the user's default.

driver

Installed SAP HANA ODBC driver name, default "HDBODBC", or a library path supported by the driver manager. Install a current SAP HANA Client with JWT authentication support.

ssl_trust_store

Optional trust-store path for the SAP HANA Client's TLS provider. NULL uses the client's configured trust store.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning an odbc DBI connection.

Details

Install odbc and SAP HANA Client's ODBC driver. Configure a JWT provider, signing-certificate trust, external-identity mappings and user privileges in the target database. The OAuth provider must issue a JWT access token accepted by this configuration. Browser SSO for SAP BTP alone does not establish SQL access. There is no universal SAP scope or token audience.

The helper supplies the token as PWD with an empty UID and restricts authenticationMethods to jwt. TLS encryption, certificate validation and matching of the endpoint hostname are required. DSNs, saved user credentials, session cookies and alternate authentication methods cannot be selected through this helper.

Create the helper inside server() and call connection <- con() before each query. Valid SQL sessions survive ordinary token renewal. Account changes, permission loss, sign-out and Shiny session end close them. Native automatic reconnect is disabled; reopen a broken connection through con() to supply a current token. Failed queries are not replayed.

See also

vignette("hana", package = "shinyOAuthDB") for sign-in, database configuration and a complete Shiny app.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_oracle(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_hana(
  auth$connection,
  server = "example.hana.prod-eu10.hanacloud.ondemand.com",
  schema = "REPORTING"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER AS DATABASE_USER FROM DUMMY")
})
} # }
